speaking.q: Some people say 'I have nothing to hide, so I don't care about privacy.' Do you agree?
Why do you think people who say privacy doesn't matter still protect their passwords and lock their doors?
Do you think constant monitoring changes the way people behave, even when nobody is actually watching?
Can one journalist or one whistleblower really move the dial on a big issue like mass surveillance?
What is the crux of the debate between privacy and security?
